messages:
incident-bot: [P1] Dedicated pool 'meridian-vpc-01' GPU utilization >95% for 7m — queue length rising, request latency p99 > 12s. Paging oncall.
oncall-ryan: I'm awake, taking it. Pulling dashboards now — link: https://monitoring.redwood/meridian-vpc-01
sre-ana: I see GPU backlog and kernel queueing. Memory pressure on a subset of nodes (node-gpu-7/8). Error rate ~8% 503s for that tenant.
oncall-ryan: Confirmed. Customer MeridianCorp reports degraded inference. ETA for impact window? support-maya, any customer chatter?
support-maya: Meridian CS says ~5% of calls failing, mainly long prompts during business hours. They're seeing timeouts at 30s.
eng-runtime-lee: Possible KV cache growth from long-chat sessions. Can we force cache eviction for that tenant temporarily? Need approval before touching tenant state.
solutions-jamie: Meridian is on enterprise SLA (SLA-99.9) and reserved pool. Account team - Kate, do we have burst allowance to shared capacity?
account-mgr-kate: Meridian contract includes emergency burst up to 10% of their committed capacity for incidents. Approve temporary burst for 20m while we mitigate. :white_check_mark:
prod-ops-victor: I'm standing by to spin up burst instances in us-east-1. Will allocate 4x A10g equivalent (hot spare) if eng-runtime approves.
eng-runtime-lee: Okay, doing a conservative plan: 1) enable burst nodes (prod-ops), 2) throttle best-effort non-enterprise traffic routed to this pool, 3) enable per-tenant cache eviction and reduce kv_cache_size to 256MB for Meridian. Applying step 3 now.
oncall-ryan: Apply throttles for low-priority routes: route IDs r-low-*/batch -> 20% throughput. Also enable fallback to quantized v1.3-small model for heavy prompts (lee can flip routing rule).
eng-runtime-lee: Flipped routing rule: heavy prompts -> model v1.3-q8. Reduced kv cache for Meridian, triggered cache GC. Spinning burst nodes now (prod-ops-victor).
incident-bot: Action log: burst nodes requested by prod-ops-victor at 3412345722, state: provisioning.
prod-ops-victor: Burst nodes up and joined pool at 3412345750. Observability: backlog dropped 60% in first 90s.
oncall-ryan: Error rate falling to 1.2%. Latency p99 down to 2.8s. Meridian CS confirms degraded UX improving.
support-maya: Meridian confirms fewer timeouts, still seeing some slow tails on very long chats; they want a postmortem.
eng-runtime-lee: Next steps: keep burst for 30m, run offline analysis of KV usage and prompt length distribution, consider per-tenant model quantization profile for long-term fix.
account-mgr-kate: I'll notify the Meridian CTO with incident update and ETA for postmortem. Log the burst usage to billing as incident credit.
oncall-ryan: Triage complete for now. Leaving follow-up tickets: INC-341234 (postmortem), TKT-341235 (runtime mitigations), TKT-341236 (billing adj). Handoff to SRE Ana for postmortem.
sre-ana: Taking handoff. Will collect traces, set a blameless postmortem and include playbook updates (runbook: dedicated-pool-pressure). ETA doc by EOD.
incident-bot: Incident resolved for MeridianCorp — metrics normalized, burst nodes drained at 3412345795. Closing alert.

[snippets]
oncall-ryan (debug command):
```
# quick check
curl -s https://monitoring.redwood/api/pool/meridian-vpc-01/metrics | jq '.gpu_util,p99_latency,queued'
```

eng-runtime-lee (note):
"If we see repeated long-chat KV growth from this tenant we should add a per-tenant max-kv-age policy and consider autoscale by active sessions instead of GPU occupancy alone."

reactions: :rotating_light: incident-bot pinned, :thumbsup: from account-mgr-kate, :zap: from eng-runtime-lee
